summary:
# NOTES: "The Chevalier's Daughter; or, An Exile for the Truth" by Lucy Ellen Guernsey (single book; no other volumes)

## Front matter
- Series head: "The Stanton-Corbet Chronicles, Year 1660." Title page: THE CHEVALIER'S DAUGHTER; OR, An Exile for the Truth, by Lucy Ellen Guernsey, author of "Lady Betty's Governess," "Winifred," "Lady Rosamond's Book." London: John F. Shaw and Co., 48 Paternoster Row. New Edition.
- Publisher ads list other Guernsey titles: Oldham; Loveday's History; The Foster Sisters; Lady Betty's Governess; Lady Rosamond's Book; Winifred; Through Unknown Ways; Chapters in our "Island Story." Also Rev. Andrew Reed's Edgar Nelthorpe, Alice Bridge of Norwich, Ida Vane.
- NOTE (editor, Rosamond Genevieve Corbet, Tre Madoc Court, May 1, 1740): memoirs written by her grandmother (Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin) in old age; papers found in carved cabinet after grandparents died within a week of each other; she transcribed them during a sprained ankle. Mentions younger brother repairing cabinet; dauphin may bring toleration.

## Main characters
- **Genevieve "Vevette" d'Antin** (narrator, b. 1660 at Tour d'Antin near Sartilly, Normandy). Later Agnes Genevieve Corbet. Dark ("true black Corby"), prone to palpitations, quick temper that cools, dreamy, double-minded.
- **Chevalier Armand d'Antin** (father): younger son of Provençal De Fayrolles family; Protestant; kind; worshipped wife; killed at Avranches by Michaud (his ex-gamekeeper he had saved from galleys). Called "my Pearl" by wife. Taught "My duty" motto. Dedicated Vevette to God's service.
- **Margaret Corbet d'Antin** (mother): English, Cornish/Devonshire Corbet; pale alabaster skin, gray eyes, black lashes, arched brows; grave, deeply religious; Protestant; prayed with Litany; died at Stanton Court (attack after rising, spring of joy/dream). Sister: Aunt Amy (Corbet, Tre Madoc). Brother: Uncle Charles (Corbet, court in London; married Aunt Jem/Jemima, who has an affected air; Aunt Jem later dies in London). Later Uncle Charles's wife Aunt Jem.
- **Simon Sablot**: tall, blue-eyed Norman farmer, foster-father, devout; calls Vevette "Vevette"/"little one"; cultivated buckwheat farm; later at Tre Madoc gardener; survives to old age.
- **Jeanne Sablot**: foster-mother, Provençal/Vaudois origins, former cook at château; "Ma bonne"; sings; cabinet ("bahut") made by her great-grandfather (doves on top, olive-leaf-in-circle sign); later cook at Tre Madoc.
- **David Sablot**: foster-brother, elder; learned shipbuilding at Dieppe; carved spinning wheel for Vevette; ran away to Granville procession (St Michael) but turned back on Vevette's words; later carpenter in Penzance; helps send message at Marseilles.
- **Lucille (Loulou/Lucille) Sablot**: foster-sister, jealous; "only a little girl" quarrel; becomes Catholic at ~age 17 after quarrel on rock; takes nuns' hospital; gives Vevette bluebottle fly "warning" via Pierre; later Mme in Canada; falls into river; survives, becomes interpreter at Boston; reunited with family; never marries.
- **Pierre Le Febre**: wild young fisherman, loved Lucille; married Isabeau; helps flight with his boat; later Jersey.
- **Grace (Mrs. Grace)**: Cornish lady-in-waiting ("Gracy", "Mamselle Grace"); lecturer; strict; ankle sprain; dies in swoon; buried in vault under ruined chapel.
- **Andrew Corbet**: cousin, destined husband; short, broad-shouldered, large nose, gray eyes that look black, black crisp hair; sailor; "Vevette is a real Corbet woman"; hawk-trainer; jealous and distrustful; made "Mitspah" seal ring (Jerusalem). Vevette gave him gold locket. Wears it still.
- **Betty Corbet** (later Mrs. Lovel/ Mrs. Charles Lovel): Andrew's sister; mischief-maker; gives book to mother; betrays meeting with Mr. Lovel; later marries him.
- **Mr. Charles Lovel**: suitor; spendthrift; unbeliever.
- **Margaret ("Meg") Corbet** (cousin, tall fair, later Mrs. Treverthy). **Rosamond Corbet** (cousin, studious, "Rosamond Genevieve Corbet" the editor, later kind). **Aunt Amy** (Mrs. Corbet, Andrew's mother).
- **Cousin Marianne**: Sister of Cousin George Corbet (rector of Jersey parish). Cousin Marianne soft-footed, "dear old lady". Cousin George: rector, white hair. Daughters Katherine, Paulina, Eleanor (nursing talent), twin boys.
- **Father Simon's wife**... (see Jeanne).
- **Monsieur Bertheau**: old pastor, lodged in tower; flight by boat; drowned later.
- **Louis de Reviere**: former companion of Armand; now Franciscan; warned family, betrayed (per mother's view mistaken).
- **Father Martien**: Jesuit confessor; educated Florence; pressures conversion; later in Canada in disguise (appears with Indians).
- **Monsieur de Fayrolles** (uncle, Marquis, Charles' sister-in-law Madame Zenobie / "Aunt Zenobie"): later "Uncle Charles" of Paris = Monsieur de Fayrolles? (uncle = Marquis de Fayrolles, Armand's elder brother, converted). Aunt Zenobie = Madame de Fayrolles, rouged, petit.
- **Monsieur de Luynes**: elderly suitor, scar, good man; Vevette refuses.
- **Zelie, Susanne** (maids): Susanne kindly; Zelie hostile.
- **Mercer**: Aunt Jem's gentlewoman; refuses to go to France; sister's school at Hackney; given devotional books.
- **Mother Mary of the Incarnation** (Ursuline, historic; Canada); Superior: "Mother St. Stanislaus"? (Sister St. Stanislaus, Sister St. Anne, Sister Joanne, Sister Margaret); Desirée (orphan, died at sea); Louisonne (nearly drowned, hid).
- **Captain Mayhew** (Good Hope, Boston); **Mr. Norton** (minister, married them); **Mr. Folsom** (magistrate); Mistress Folsom.

## Places
- Tour d'Antin (Normandy, reddish stone; square & round towers; chapel; ghost of white chevalier; secret passage; carved bahut); Sartilly; Granville; Avranches; Mont St. Michel; the Grève (sands); Jersey; Tre Madoc (Cornwall); Tre Madoc Court; Well House (St. Wenna's Well); Stanton Court (Devonshire, near Biddeford); Allinstree (Puritan father-in-law); Exeter; London (Covent Garden); Paris; Fontainebleau; Marseilles (Ursuline convent); Boston; Hampton (New England farm); Dieppe; Charenton; Honfleur.

## Key events (in order)
1. Birth 1660; Jeanne nurses her; Lucille/David; David runs to Granville procession; Simon's warning on images; "only a little girl" quarrel.
2. Vevette returns to Tour d'Antin; Mrs. Grace; the curé's wolves warning; hospital of St Jacques (nuns) opens at Sartilly.
3. Youth: stolen play book; mother's punishment; Hackluyt voyages; hospital fever/fire/flood; persecution narrative.
4. Lucille's jealousy; rock talk; procession of nuns; Lucille "Why did they not trust me"; Grace's fall; father entrusts pastor Bertheau; chapel secret stone.
5. Night: Vevette leads pastor; Lucille apostasy on rock (gilded crucifix). Lucille's cruel note.
6. Andrew arrives; lonely grange Lord's Supper; pastor leaves, boat drowned.
7. Procession; Lucille and Luchon girl; storm; Grace dies; buried in vault.
8. Flight: Andrew & Armand to Avranches; Armand killed; Lucille's bluebottle "fly" warning via Pierre; mob attacks tower; Michaud falls through floor; Blanchon the white cat; escape by boat to Jersey.
9. Jersey: Cousin Marianne, Cousin George; Vevette ill for weeks; mother's health fails.
10. London, Pepys, uncle Charles and Aunt Jem; Vevette's pride; jewels sold; Simon & Jeanne found in Threadneedle Street.
11. Tre Madoc: Aunt Amy; Betty's mischief; Well House; Dinah (foundling, Vaudois dove).
12. Book episode; Betty & Mr Lovel; Vevette breaks; mother to Stanton Court; mother dies there.
13. Stanton Court: Lord Stanton (guardian), Lady Stanton, Lewis (young lord), Martha, Theo (marries Dean of Exeter), Captain Bernard, Betty's false tales; Vevette goes to London.
14. London: Aunt Jem; Father Martien; Aunt Jem dies; Vevette converts; Paris; retreat; Monsieur de Luynes refused; attic prison; Marseilles; David; sent to Canada.
15. Ursuline convent; ship; storm; Good Hope; Andrew (Captain's ship) marries Vevette at sea by Mr. Norton; Boston; Lucille found as interpreter.
16. Conclusion: six years at Hampton; Father Martien seen with Indians; return to Cornwall; fates: Lucille, David, Betty, Uncle Charles, Monsieur de Fayrolles (duel), Zenobie (convent), Susanne, Lord & Lady Stanton, Lewis, Theo, Margaret, Rosamond.
17. Closing: "A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways." (St. James 1:8); "If any man love the world..." (1 John 2:15); "Ye cannot serve God and mammon." (Matt. 6:24). Signed Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin.

## Notable phrases
- "My duty" (father's motto). "Ah, if your father were but here!" (mother). "Vevette is a real Corbet woman." "Balancez vous donc." "Ye cannot serve God and mammon."
